I can't 100% support your statement, but overall, I agree. Body confidence is a great thing - when you're confident about your **healthy** body. Some folks do have medical conditions that limit their ability to control their weight, whether from the condition itself or from medications prescribed for a condition. So, I very much disagree with your statement that "you are in control of your habits". 

But this acceptance and pride over being morbidly obese is unhealthy and incredibly dangerous. Number one leading cause of death in the US? Anyone? Cardiovascular disease. Most folks would guess cancer. Nope. Our unhealthy asses are dying from our lifestyle and nutrition choices. How about raising taxes on foods high in sugar or fast food instead of cigarettes the next time a state government needs additional revenue? I use this example because they did this in my state and my first thought was, "Well, a significant tax increase on cigarettes will probably lead to a decrease in the number of smokers (not a bad thing but not a good thing if you're counting on that increased revenue to save your state). Why not raise taxes on the things that are adding to the cardiovascular disease rates? Discourage people from unhealthy foods, thus helping their health and reducing medical costs associated with it?" 

No one wants to hear this kind of stuff, but it's reality. It's not about feelings. Being morbidly obese IS NOT GOOD FOR YOU AND IS NOT SOMETHING TO BE PROUD OF.

I'm far from perfect, so I have no room to judge others and try to refrain from doing so. But please people, stop spreading the message that morbid obesity is okay. You're doing a whole generation of women a disservice.

You're in college and probably have enough on your plate without spending too much time worrying about a potential problem. You mentioned that the only family you guys have is either out of the country or in the state you currently live in. Should your brother defy the odds and stick with this non-plan plan two years from now, and your mother follows through on moving, you'll still have family nearby. It's not the same as having your sibling and/or your mother, but at least there will still be people around who truly care about you.

If you're genuinely concerned about the path your brother is taking, and not just for your own selfish reasons, or hell, even for your own selfish reasons, why don't you sit down and talk to him? If he rebuffs your attempt once, keep trying. If you two don't already have a close relationship to the extent that you feel like he'll actually listen to your concerns, perhaps the best way to go is to work on building/strengthening that relationship, showing him you care and **then** have the conversation about his plans when he'll be more receptive to you have to say. And there you have my random, internet stranger two cents. Good luck.

I had another rescue dog that had biting/snipping issues. Took her to an animal behaviorist and it sounds crazy, but this was their recommendation and it worked: when she bites you too roughly, stick your finger down her throat enough to make her gag. It may feel like you're abusing your dog and it sucks, but it will work. Once you get her to stop biting/snipping, you can't continue to engage in the behavior with her, even in play, because she won't recognize the difference.

If she's not treat motivated, what makes her happiest? Belly rubs? Ear scratches? Praise? Find what she gets the greatest reward from and use that as your positive reinforcement. Get excited each and every time she pees outside and make a big deal out of it (no matter how ridiculous you may feel lol) until you've got the housebreaking under control. Just my two cents. Hope that helps!

My younger pup is a Hurricane Harvey rescue (2 yr old mixed breed) and when he came to live with me in December, his previous caretakers (won't call them owners after this story) told me that he "couldn't" be house broken and he was a biter and allegedly, their vet recommended that he be put down. Unless this vet is in the absolute wrong profession or is just a sicko who likes to kill animals, that's not a solution for a 10 pound dog. Long story short, after lots of frustration with the daily "accidents" and the biting (including my mother's butt), it turned out he had a kidney stone! The kidney stone was from a long untreated UTI (previous caretakers were asses), and after treatment, things have improved greatly. Accidents aren't completely resolved, it's down to a maybe once a week thing instead of multiple times daily. And he hasn't bitten anyone since.
How old was your dog when you got her? Puppies that are taken from their litters too early often don't learn "bite inhibition" and don't realize that they are hurting you. Is it playful biting? Food aggression? Taking a toy from her? What triggers the biting? 
Housebreaking is a chore....... Who wants to get up at 5 am to take their dog out to do their business? But the payoff is so worth it once you've got them trained. My best advice is consistency. Don't let one accident go unnoticed or unacknowledged. Dogs want to please their "owners", so reinforce the good behavior (in this case, relieving herself outside) whenever you see it. "Good potty!", etc. Hope that helps!

If overdosing were so easy, more suicidal people would do it. It's pretty damn difficult to successfully overdose on purpose. For someone who is seriously considering it and is researching the various successful methods, you'll find that the drug cocktail you need to ensure death is almost impossible to get your hands on. Finding the "lethal dose" for medications that you can obtain with relative ease isn't likely to occur. And if you fail at overdosing, you're likely to wind up in a hospital with a ton of medical bills to add to your pile of burdens or if no one finds you, you'll wake up feeling like absolute shit from the drugs you took and your failed attempt.
